unit.can_do_en: start and end a phone call and leave a message.

brief.situation_en: Maria calls the wrong person. Esa answers.

judge.reason: Moi/hei greeting, onks/onko, tää/tämä are only register differences.
Ei oo/Ei ole is the same negation; the rest is identical.

lines.speaker: Maria
lines.text_puhe: Voi anteeks! Mul on väärä numero.
lines.text_kirja: Voi anteeksi! Minulla on väärä numero.
lines.gloss_en: Oh, sorry! I have the wrong number.

judge.reason: anteeks/anteeksi and mul/minulla are register variants; same meaning.

puhe.text: Voi anteeks! Mul on väärä numero.

kirja.text: Voi anteeksi! Minulla on väärä numero.

lines.speaker: Esa
lines.text_puhe: Ei se mitään. Mihin numeroon sä soitit?
lines.text_kirja: Ei se mitään. Mihin numeroon sinä soitit?
lines.gloss_en: No problem. Which number did you call?

judge.reason: sä/sinä is only a register difference; the rest is identical.

puhe.text: Ei se mitään. Mihin numeroon sä soitit?

kirja.text: Ei se mitään. Mihin numeroon sinä soitit?

lines.speaker: Maria
lines.text_puhe: Nolla neljä nolla, kuus kuus kuus...
lines.text_kirja: Nolla neljä nolla, kuusi kuusi kuusi...

judge.reason: kuus/kuusi is the spoken form of six; the digits are the same.

puhe.text: Nolla neljä nolla, kuus kuus kuus...

kirja.text: Nolla neljä nolla, kuusi kuusi kuusi...

lines.speaker: Esa
lines.text_puhe: Mun numero alkaa nolla neljä viis.
lines.text_kirja: Minun numeroni alkaa nolla neljä viisi.

judge.reason: Mun numero/minun numeroni and viis/viisi are register variants; the digits are the same.

puhe.text: Mun numero alkaa nolla neljä viis.

kirja.text: Minun numeroni alkaa nolla neljä viisi.

lines.speaker: Maria
lines.gloss_en: Ah, OK. Thanks for the help!

judge.reason: Aa/Ai, okei/selvä and kiitti/kiitos are interjections and register variants; the thanks for the help is the same.
Moikka and Kuulemiin are both goodbyes, a difference of register only; Ole hyvä is the same.

forms.why_en: Moi is the everyday spoken hello. Books and formal texts write hei.

forms.form_name_en: present tense, 3rd person singular, with the question ending -ko/-kö
forms.why_en: On with -ko to ask a question. Speech often says -ks: onks.
Speech shortens tämä to tää. Books write tämä.
Ei on its own answers 'no'. People say it the same way.
After ei the verb drops its ending: olla becomes ole. Speech shortens ole to oo.
This is the dictionary form. People say it the same way.
This is the dictionary form. People say it the same way.
Speech drops the final i: anteeksi becomes anteeks.
Minä with -lla. With on it means 'I have'. Speech shortens it to mul.
The form of olla, to be, for he, she or it. People say it the same way.
This is the dictionary form. People say it the same way.
This is the dictionary form. People say it the same way.
This is the dictionary form. People say it the same way.
The partitive singular of mikään 'any': mitään. 'Ei se mitään' means 'it's nothing, no problem'.
Mikä with -hin for 'to': mihin, where to.
Adds -on for 'into, to': numero becomes numeroon, 'which number did you call'.
Speech shortens sinä to sä. Books write sinä.
Adds -i for the past and -t for 'you': soittaa becomes soitit, tt turning to t.
This is the dictionary form. People say it the same way.
This is the dictionary form. People say it the same way.
Speech drops the final i: kuusi becomes kuus.
Minä with -n: minun pitää means I have to. Speech shortens it to mun.

forms.form_name_en: nominative singular, with the possessive ending for my
forms.why_en: Adds -ni for 'my': numero becomes numeroni. Speech just says mun numero.
This is the dictionary form. People say it the same way.
Speech drops the final i: viisi becomes viis.
Speech often says aa for ai, ah.
Okei is the everyday spoken OK. Books write selvä, which means clear.
Kiitti is the everyday spoken thanks. Books write kiitos.
Apu, help, with -sta: avusta, and p turns to v. Kiitos takes -sta for 'thanks for'.
The imperative for one person is olla without its ending: ole. 'Ole hyvä' means 'here you are' or 'you're welcome'.
This is the dictionary form. People say it the same way.
Kuulemiin is the polite goodbye on the phone. In everyday speech people say moikka instead.
